info.bio:
Danzig es un grupo de heavy metal, fundado por su vocalista Glenn Danzig en 1987 tras su salida de The Misfits y Samhain.

La alineación original estaba conformada por Chuck Biscuits en batería, John Christ en guitarra, Eerie Von en bajo, y Glenn Danzig en voz. Aunque técnicamente se podrían clasificar como heavy metal, sus primeros discos tienen profundas influencias de blues. La voz de Glenn Danzig es grave, profunda y potente, con un timbre que recuerda en algunas de sus canciones a Elvis Presley o a Jim Morrison.

scenes.name: Cruces del punk: de Fugazi al punk-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: A finales de los ochenta el punk es el más vivo de los subgéneros del rock: miles de bandas ensayando en garajes, un lenguaje universal como no se veía desde los sesenta. Nueva York: Adrenalin O.D., el straight-edge de Youth Of Today y Gorilla Biscuits, el crossover punk-metal (Cro-Mags, Prong, Danzig). Washington lanza a Pussy Galore (la irrelevancia hecha relevante), Unrest y Fugazi de Ian MacKaye, que abstrae el hardcore en una forma teatral de compromiso ético y estético (Repeater, Steady Diet Of Nothing, Red Medicine), y Royal Trux (Twin Infinitives, «un Trout Mask Replica para la generación grunge»). El punk-pop de Mr T Experience, Dwarves, Henry Rollins, L7 (pioneras del «foxcore»), Lemonheads, Screeching Weasel, Goo Goo Dolls, Fastbacks, Shonen Knife; el «rogue folk» de los Pogues, Membranes y Chumbawamba.

xref.title: Deep Depression Post-Nirvana (1994)
xref.body: Following Kurt Cobain's death in April 1994, Dave Grohl entered a period of deep depression and was unsure of his future in music. He seriously considered quitting music entirely or joining another band, having received invitations from Danzig and Tom Petty. However, he realized he didn't want to be "just a drummer," as playing drums would constantly remind him of his time in Nirvana, a painful memory at that point. "Give it up music actually was an option for a while."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Desert Session Projects – Produced by Eleven Members
xref.body: Josh Homme's Desert Session projects received production assistance from Elaine Johannes and Natasha Schneider of the band Eleven, following their work on Chris Cornell's solo album. This collaboration brought Johannes and Schneider into contact with members from various other prominent bands, including A Perfect Circle, Nine Inch Nails, Danzig, Marilyn Manson's band, and PJ Harvey. xref.title: Formation and Longevity
xref.body: Glenn Danzig founded the Misfits around 1976 and kept the band active for six years, during which they developed their unique blend of hardcore, horror movie aesthetics, and metal. "The main guy was Glenn Danzig, who started the band somewhere around 1976, armed with his own indie record label. Danzig kept the Missfits going for six years, blending hardcore with horror movies and metal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation and Style
xref.body: The Misfits were formed around 1976 by Glenn Danzig in New Jersey. They maintained their presence for six years, distinctively blending hardcore with themes from horror movies and elements of metal. "The Missfits were from Jersey. The main guy was Glenn Danzig, who started the band somewhere around 1976. Armed with his own indie record label. And as he kept the misfits going for six years, blending hardcore with horror movies and metal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Producers for Chris Cornell's Solo Album – Launchpad for Other Gigs
xref.body: The group Eleven, comprising Elaine Johannes and Natasha Schneider, played a crucial role in producing Chris Cornell's debut solo record, *Euphoria Morning*. Their work on this album garnered them further producing gigs for notable artists like No Doubt and Josh Homme's Desert Session projects, connecting them to members of A Perfect Circle, Nine Inch Nails, Danzig, Marilyn Manson's band, and PJ Harvey. "Chris reliant on both of them to help produce his debut solo record Euphoria Morning... who, based on this work, got producing gigs for no doubt in Josh Hommie in the early days of his desert session projects."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
